title: Section 199 — Public servant disobeying direction under law

content.overview: Section 199 — Public servant disobeying direction under law. The operative rule is the text of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Cite the BNS section, not the repealed Indian Penal Code, for conduct governed by the BNS. Public servant disobeying direction under law. Historical concordance: IPC 166A. For conduct governed by the BNS, cite BNS section 199; the IPC reference is historical concordance. Punishment, ingredients and exceptions are only those the section states. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
199. Whoever, being a public servant,—
(a) knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other matter; or
(b) knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation; or
(c) fails to record any information given to him under sub-section (1) of section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in relation to cognizable offence punishable under section 64, section 65, section 66, section 67, section 68, section 70, section 71, section 74, section 76, section 77, section 79, section 124, section 143 or section 144,
shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 199 constitutes a key component of Chapter XII (Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing public servant disobeying direction under law. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of public servant disobeying direction under law under Section 199 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 199.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 199 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 199 vs General Attempt: Section 199 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 199 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 199 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants.
